chunks: And from him, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man reaches the age of forty, it is said to him: 'Take caution, for you are without excuse.' And the forty-year-old is not more entitled to caution than the twenty-year-old, for what seeks them both is the same (death), and it is not sleeping. So work for what is in front of you from the horrors, and set aside useless speech.

key_terms.الْهَوْل: The horrors or terrors of the Day of Judgment and the grave.
key_terms.حِذْر: Caution or vigilance regarding one's spiritual state and deeds.
key_terms.غَيْرُ مَعْذُورٍ: Without excuse; no longer excused for ignorance or negligence.
key_terms.فُضُولَ الْقَوْلِ: Useless or frivolous speech that distracts from remembrance of God.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of reaching the age of forty in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) highlights the age of forty as a critical threshold where negligence is no longer excused, urging believers to adopt *hithr* (vigilance) regardless of age. He emphasizes that the pursuit of the afterlife is constant and active, advising the faithful to focus on essential deeds and curtail frivolous speech to prepare for the inevitable encounter with death.

en.hubeali:
And from him, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a man comes to the age of forty it is said to him: ‘Take a caution, for you are without an excuse’, and there is no person of forty (years of age) more rightful with the caution than a person of twenty, for what is seeking them both, is the one (death) and it is not sleeping. Therefore, work for what is in front of you from the horrors and stay away from the useless speech’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) in a marfu’ manner from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When a man reaches the age of forty it is said to him, ‘Beware, you have no excuses!’ In fact, a person at the age of forty is not obliged to exercise caution against sins more than the person at the age of twenty. What is after both of them is the same (that is death) and it is not sleeping. Perform good deeds for what lies ahead of frightening conditions and stop the unnecessary words.’”
